capsuleTopic.title: Solomon
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Wisdom · Temple · kingship · divided heart · memory
capsuleTopic.orientation: Follow Solomon from a loved child and contested successor through wisdom, administration, Temple building, prayer, wealth, divided loyalty, death, attributed voices, and later memory. Keep parallel accounts, literary headings, and later interpretation distinct.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Notice what Solomon inherits, asks, builds, orders, accumulates, prays, fails to keep, and becomes in later Scripture.

payload.description: Labor, materials, measurements, craftsmanship, palace construction, and the Temple’s furnishings make royal building visible.

nodes.note: Solomon and Hiram arrange timber, food, skilled work, forced labor, and stone preparation for the Temple.
nodes.title: Solomon contracts for cedar and labor

nodes.note: Solomon builds the house with chambers and carefully prepared stone; God speaks about dwelling among Israel if Solomon obeys.
nodes.title: The Temple rises under a covenant word

nodes.note: The inner rooms are lined, carved, overlaid, partitioned, and furnished with large cherubim.
nodes.title: Wood, gold, and cherubim fill the interior

nodes.note: Solomon spends thirteen years on royal buildings, including the Forest of Lebanon, judgment hall, residence, and a house for Pharaoh’s daughter.
nodes.title: Solomon builds his palace complex

nodes.note: Huram makes pillars, capitals, the sea, stands, basins, and bronze work; Solomon supplies gold furnishings and brings David’s dedicated gifts.
nodes.title: Huram fashions the Temple vessels

nodes.note: Solomon requests a skilled worker and timber from Huram, acknowledges that heaven cannot contain God, and numbers resident foreigners for labor.
nodes.title: Solomon prepares a great house

nodes.note: Chronicles locates the Temple at Moriah and describes dimensions, gold, cherubim, veil, and pillars.
nodes.title: The house is built on Mount Moriah

nodes.note: The altar, sea, basins, lampstands, tables, courts, utensils, and doors are made in prescribed metals and placements.
nodes.title: The bronze and gold work is completed

payload.title: Building the house

payload.description: The ark enters the Temple, glory fills it, Solomon prays, sacrifices are offered, and the people celebrate.

nodes.note: Solomon assembles Israel, priests bring the ark, a cloud fills the house, and Solomon blesses the assembly.
nodes.title: The ark enters and glory fills the house

nodes.note: Solomon praises covenant faithfulness, asks the promise to David to continue, and asks God to hear prayers directed toward the house.
nodes.title: Solomon asks the uncontainable God to hear

nodes.note: The prayer asks God to judge, forgive, teach, send rain, hear foreigners, support battle, and restore exiles.
nodes.title: Solomon prays across guilt, disaster, exile, and foreigners

nodes.note: Solomon blesses the assembly, urges wholehearted obedience, offers many sacrifices, and celebrates fourteen days.
nodes.title: Solomon blesses the people and holds the feast

nodes.note: The ark enters, singers and trumpeters praise God’s goodness and covenant love, and the cloud fills the house.
nodes.title: Singers and trumpeters accompany the glory

nodes.note: Solomon blesses Israel, recounts David’s desire and his own building, kneels with spread hands, and asks God to hear.
nodes.title: Solomon kneels before the assembly

nodes.note: Solomon asks for judgment, forgiveness, rain, relief, foreigner inclusion, victory, and return from exile, ending with an appeal for the anointed.
nodes.title: Petitions move toward exile and the anointed king

nodes.note: Fire consumes the offerings, glory fills the house, and the people bow while musicians and sacrifices accompany the festival.
nodes.title: Fire falls and the people worship

payload.title: Ark, prayer, and dedication

payload.description: Foreign marriages, other gods, adversaries, Jeroboam, death notices, and later memory expose the reign’s fracture.

nodes.note: Solomon loves many foreign women, builds high places, and follows other gods; the LORD announces that the kingdom will be torn.
nodes.title: Solomon’s heart turns toward other gods

nodes.note: The LORD raises adversaries from Edom and Aram whose histories reach back through David’s wars and regional violence.
nodes.title: Hadad and Rezon become adversaries

nodes.note: Ahijah tears a new garment, gives ten pieces to Jeroboam, explains Solomon’s breach, and offers Jeroboam a conditional house.
nodes.title: Ahijah gives ten pieces to Jeroboam

nodes.note: The book of Solomon’s acts is cited; Solomon dies and is buried, and Rehoboam reigns.
nodes.title: Solomon dies after forty years

nodes.note: Prophetic records are cited; Solomon dies after forty years and Rehoboam succeeds him.
nodes.title: Chronicles closes Solomon’s reign

nodes.note: Sirach remembers peace, wisdom, songs, wealth, sexual surrender, defilement, divided kingdom, and a surviving remnant.
nodes.title: Sirach praises and indicts Solomon

payload.title: Divided loyalty and the end of the reign

payload.description: Later Scripture remembers Solomon through warning, genealogy, splendor, wisdom, Temple critique, and the division inherited by Rehoboam.

nodes.note: Nehemiah confronts Judeans over foreign marriages and cites Solomon as a beloved king led into sin by foreign women.
nodes.title: Nehemiah uses Solomon as a warning

nodes.note: Matthew traces David’s line through the wife of Uriah to Solomon, then through Rehoboam.
nodes.title: Solomon enters Jesus’ genealogy

nodes.note: Jesus points to lilies clothed by God and says Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of them.
nodes.title: Jesus compares lilies with Solomon’s glory

nodes.note: Jesus refuses a demanded sign except Jonah’s and says the queen of the south will judge the generation because she came to hear Solomon’s wisdom.
nodes.title: Jesus speaks of one greater than Solomon

nodes.note: Jesus calls the generation evil, names Jonah as sign, and says the queen came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon.
nodes.title: Luke pairs Solomon with Jonah

nodes.note: Stephen recalls the wilderness tent, David’s desire, Solomon’s building, and Isaiah’s claim that the Most High does not dwell in handmade houses.
nodes.title: Stephen places Solomon’s house under prophetic critique

nodes.note: Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon’s hard service; he rejects elder counsel, threatens heavier burdens, and the northern tribes revolt.
nodes.title: Rehoboam rejects the plea for lighter service

nodes.note: The assembly asks for relief from Solomon’s heavy yoke; Rehoboam follows young counselors and Israel rebels.
nodes.title: Chronicles retells the kingdom’s division

nodes.note: Josiah defiles Topheth, removes royal horses and chariots dedicated to the sun, destroys altars, and defiles the high places Solomon built for foreign gods.
nodes.title: Josiah destroys Solomon’s high places

nodes.note: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, removes Temple and palace treasures, and cuts up the gold articles Solomon made.
nodes.title: Babylon cuts up Solomon’s gold work

nodes.note: Babylon burns the LORD’s house and Jerusalem, breaks the bronze work, and carries its metal to Babylon.
nodes.title: The Temple is burned and bronze is carried away

nodes.note: After Rehoboam abandons the instruction, Egypt invades; leaders humble themselves, Jerusalem is spared from total destruction, and treasures and gold shields are taken.
nodes.title: Shishak takes the Temple and palace treasures

nodes.note: Judah and visiting Israelites celebrate Passover with music, teaching, confession, and extended feasting; Chronicles says Jerusalem had not known such joy since Solomon.
nodes.title: Hezekiah’s Passover recalls Solomon’s joy

nodes.note: A collected letter recalls cloud and glory at the Temple, Solomon’s dedication, fire consuming sacrifice, and Moses’ earlier offering.
nodes.title: A later Temple memory recalls Solomon’s sacrifice

nodes.note: Jesus directs disciples from anxiety to ravens and lilies, saying Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one flower.
nodes.title: Luke remembers Solomon’s glory among the lilies

nodes.note: The interpreting angel identifies the transformed woman as Zion, the city Solomon built, and explains her grief through the Temple’s fall.
nodes.title: The mourning woman becomes Solomon’s city

nodes.note: During Rehoboam’s reign, Judah multiplies high places and Shishak takes Temple and palace treasures, including Solomon’s gold shields.
nodes.title: Kings remembers Solomon’s gold becoming bronze

nodes.note: Manasseh rebuilds high places, worships the sky’s army, practices occult rites, and installs an Asherah image in the house named to David and Solomon.
nodes.title: Manasseh places an image in the house

nodes.note: Chronicles reports Manasseh’s altars, occult practices, child sacrifice, and idol in the house tied to David and Solomon.
nodes.title: Chronicles retells Manasseh’s Temple defilement

nodes.note: Josiah orders priests and Levites for Passover, places the ark in the house Solomon built, and refers to written divisions associated with David and Solomon.
nodes.title: Josiah restores an order linked to Solomon

nodes.note: The account of Josiah’s Passover places the ark in Solomon’s house and orders Levitical service according to David’s writing and Solomon’s magnificence.
nodes.title: 1 Esdras remembers Solomon’s Temple order

nodes.note: Ezra asks whether the righteous can intercede after judgment and names Solomon among earlier figures who prayed for others in the present age.
nodes.title: Solomon’s prayer becomes an example of intercession

nodes.note: A mother remembers a father teaching Scripture and declaring a proverb of Solomon about a tree of life among examples of faithful endurance.
nodes.title: Solomon’s proverbs enter a martyr family’s memory

nodes.title: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon

nodes.note: Solomon receives enormous gold, makes shields and a throne, acquires luxury goods, and multiplies chariots and imported horses.
nodes.title: Gold, shields, throne, chariots, and horses accumulate

nodes.note: The queen tests Solomon, praises his wisdom and Israel’s God, gives gifts, and receives royal generosity.
nodes.title: Chronicles retells the queen’s visit

nodes.note: Gold, shields, throne, vessels, ships, gifts, chariots, and horses display Solomon’s international reach.
nodes.title: Chronicles gathers the wealth report

nodes.note: The psalm asks God to give the king justice, defend the poor, crush oppression, extend peace, receive tribute, and bless all nations.
nodes.title: A royal prayer asks for justice and peace

payload.description: God answers the dedication while Solomon’s projects, labor system, fleet, and exchanges with Hiram continue.

nodes.note: God says the house is consecrated and the dynasty will endure with faithful walking, but apostasy will bring removal and ruin.
nodes.title: God answers Solomon with promise and warning

nodes.note: Solomon exchanges cities with Hiram, builds fortified centers, levies forced labor from subject peoples, and sends a fleet for gold.
nodes.title: Cities, labor, and a fleet extend the reign

nodes.note: God promises to hear humble repentance, establishes the conditional dynasty, and warns that abandonment will make the house an astonishment.
nodes.title: Chronicles expands the answer to the prayer

nodes.note: Solomon rebuilds cities, assigns forced labor, moves Pharaoh’s daughter, orders priestly service, and develops a fleet with Huram.
nodes.title: Solomon’s projects and worship order continue

nodes.note: Bathsheba bears a son named Solomon; the LORD loves him and sends the name Jedidiah through Nathan.
nodes.title: Solomon is born and named Jedidiah

nodes.note: David identifies the future Temple site, gathers foreign workers and materials, tells Solomon that the promised son of rest will build, and commands Israel’s leaders to help.
nodes.title: David prepares and charges Solomon to build

nodes.note: David names Solomon as the chosen builder and calls him to know God, serve wholeheartedly, and seek God.
nodes.title: David presents Solomon before Israel

nodes.note: David gives Solomon plans, weights, divisions, and a pattern received by the Spirit, then points to workers and leaders.
nodes.title: David gives plans and assignments

nodes.note: David gives from royal and personal treasure and invites leaders to consecrate themselves by giving.
nodes.title: Leaders give willingly for the house

nodes.note: The assembly worships, offers sacrifices, and makes Solomon king a second time; Solomon sits on the LORD’s throne.
nodes.title: Solomon is enthroned before the LORD

nodes.note: Adonijah exalts himself, gathers supporters, sacrifices, and excludes Solomon while Nathan and Bathsheba alert David.
nodes.title: Adonijah acts as king

nodes.note: David orders Solomon placed on the royal mule and anointed; the city rejoices while Adonijah’s gathering dissolves.
nodes.title: Solomon is anointed at Gihon

nodes.note: David commands courage and covenant obedience, recalls the promise, and gives instructions concerning Joab, Barzillai’s sons, and Shimei.
nodes.title: David gives Solomon a final charge

nodes.note: Adonijah is executed after requesting Abishag, Abiathar is removed, Joab is killed, Benaiah is elevated, and Shimei dies after breaking an oath.
nodes.title: Solomon consolidates the throne

nodes.note: David praises God as giver of kingdom, riches, and strength, says the people have given what already belongs to God, and asks for Solomon to receive a whole heart to obey and build.
nodes.title: David asks for Solomon’s whole heart

nodes.note: Solomon makes a marriage alliance with Egypt and loves the LORD, yet sacrifices at high places before the Temple is built.
nodes.title: Solomon marries Pharaoh’s daughter

nodes.title: Solomon asks for a listening heart

nodes.title: A judgment reveals royal wisdom

nodes.title: Solomon orders the kingdom

nodes.note: Judah and Israel are numerous and secure while Solomon rules, receives tribute, maintains a large table, and keeps horses.
nodes.title: Abundance and provision sustain the court

nodes.note: God gives Solomon breadth of mind; he speaks proverbs and songs and studies plants and animals.
nodes.title: Solomon’s wisdom reaches the nations

nodes.note: Solomon and the assembly worship at Gibeon; God invites a request and grants wisdom, knowledge, wealth, and honor.
nodes.title: Chronicles remembers the request for wisdom

nodes.note: Solomon gathers chariots and horsemen, makes silver common, and imports horses and chariots through royal traders.
nodes.title: Chariots, gold, and trade accumulate
